chunks: And with the preceding chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Rifa'ah, who reported that Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, may Allah's blessings be upon them both, said:
There are four admonitions in the Torah and four others alongside them:

Whoever rises in the morning sorrowful about worldly affairs has indeed risen displeased with his Lord. Whoever rises in the morning complaining about a misfortune that has befallen him is in reality complaining against his Lord. Whoever goes to a rich man and humbles himself before him in order to gain from his worldly wealth loses two-thirds of his faith. And whoever among the reciters of the Quran in this community enters the Hellfire, he is among those who took the signs of God as mockery and play.
And the other four are: Whoever holds absolute power will appropriate for himself; whoever consults will never regret; as you treat others, so shall you be treated; and poverty is the greatest death.

key_terms.استأثر: To monopolize, to appropriate exclusively for oneself
key_terms.التوراة: The Torah - the scripture revealed to Prophet Moses (AS)
key_terms.الفقر الموت الأكبر: Poverty is the greatest death - a profound statement about the spiritual devastation of poverty
key_terms.ساخطا: Displeased, angry - expressing discontent with divine decree

ai.seo_question: What are the eight admonitions from the Torah mentioned by Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits eight moral admonitions attributed to the Torah, divided into two groups of four. The first group warns against grief over worldly matters (which implies displeasure with God's decree), complaining about misfortunes (which amounts to complaining against God), humbling oneself before the wealthy for material gain (which destroys faith), and mockery of divine scripture. The second group offers wisdom about the corrupting nature of power, the value of consultation, reciprocity in dealings, and the spiritual devastation of poverty.
word_analysis: And with the chain of narration

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 15. And with the preceding chains of narration, from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Rafaa’h who reported that: Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, said: "
The Torah has four admonitions coupled with the other four.

They are: He who rises in the morning sorrowful about his worldly affairs, he indeed rises displeased with his Lord! And he who rises in the morning complaining about the misfortune he has suffered, he is complaining against Allah! He who calls upon a rich man, humbling himself so as to gain a share from his wealth, loses two-third of his faith; And if ever a reciter of the Qur’an in this Ummah enters hellfire, then he must be among those who take divine signs for a mockery and play.
And the other four are: Absolute power leads to appropriation; and he who consults, never repents; and you shall reap what you sow, and poverty is the greater death."
